title: Developer Experience: SDK Guides, Quickstarts, API Examples, Docs Site Ops, and Top Support Issues
author: Asha Kapoor
body:
Overview:
This page defines the operating procedures and canonical content patterns for Redwood Inference developer-facing documentation maintained by Eng: Developer Experience. It covers SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, API examples, docs-site publishing procedures, and the canonical fixes for our top support issues. The intent is to make docs consistent, discoverable, and easy for engineers and external developers to use in production integrations.

Scope and audience:
- Scope: SDK reference guides (Python, Node, Go), quickstarts and templates (chat, completions, embeddings), API examples (curl + SDK snippets), docs-site operating procedures, and triaged top support issues with canonical fixes.
- Primary audience: software engineers, ML engineers, solutions engineers, and support engineers.

Ownership and contacts:
- Content owner: Eng - Developer Experience (owner_team: engineering).
- Primary author: Asha Kapoor (DevEx).
- Reviewers: Marcus Li (SDK), Elena Rodriguez (API), Priya Nambiar (Support).
- Support escalation: devexp@redwood.ai, oncall channel #devex-docs.

Standards and style guidelines (must follow):
1. Tone: technical, concise, actionable. Avoid marketing language in examples.
2. Structure: short intro, prerequisites, step-by-step quickstart, code examples, troubleshooting, and related pages.
3. File names: kebab-case, short and descriptive (e.g., sdk-python-quickstart-chat-2026.json).
4. Examples: provide at least one curl and one SDK example for each API surface. Use realistic but anonymized keys (REDACTED_API_KEY).
5. Tests: each quickstart must include a CI check (smoke test script) referenced in the document.

Docs site operating procedures (publishing workflow):
1. Drafting: Create page in the eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates space with a clear title and prerequisite list.
2. Internal review: assign two reviewers (SDK owner + API owner). Use the reviewers field and wait for both approvals.
3. Pre-publish checks:
   - Validate code snippets run locally and in CI (unit smoke test).
   - Confirm curl + Python + Node examples produce comparable outputs.
   - Lint markdown/Confluence formatting and run link-checker.
4. Publish: set status to "published" and add labels: devexp, sdk, quickstart.
5. Post-publish monitoring: add page to the weekly docs digest; monitor support tickets for the first 30 days.
6. Versioning and updates: include a changelog section for any breaking example changes.

Content templates (required fields for every quickstart):
- Title
- Short description (1-2 sentences)
- Prerequisites (SDK version, account level, runtime requirements)
- Quickstart steps (numbered)
- Code samples (curl, Python, Node)
- Expected output (exact sample response)
- Troubleshooting section (symptoms and fixes)
- References / related pages

Canonical quickstart example (chat completion) - snippet (primary example must appear in every quickstart):
1) Prerequisites:
   - Python 3.10+, node 18+, SDKs: redwood-python >= 0.8.0, redwood-js >= 0.8.0
   - API key: REDWOOD_API_KEY (environment variable)
2) Steps:
   1. Install: pip install redwood-inference or npm install @redwood/inference
   2. Run example: python chat_quickstart.py

3) curl example:
   curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat 
     -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED_API_KEY" 
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
     -d '{"model":"redwood-chat-1","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are a helpful assistant."},{"role":"user","content":"Summarize the following text: ..."}]}'

4) Python SDK example:
   from redwood import Client
   client = Client(api_key="REDACTED_API_KEY")
   resp = client.chat.create(model="redwood-chat-1", messages=[{"role":"system","content":"You are a helpful assistant."},{"role":"user","content":"Summarize the following text: ..."}])
   print(resp.choices[0].message.content)

5) Expected output:
   - A short summary of the input text (2-4 sentences). Example: "The text describes..."

Top support issues and canonical fixes (triaged and verified):
- Issue 1: SDK auth failures after key rotation
  - Symptom: 401 Unauthorized from all SDKs immediately after customer rotated keys in the Console.
  - Root cause: Cached credentials in long-running worker processes (prefix caching + env var not reloaded).
  - Canonical fix: Instruct customers to restart long-running workers or implement token re-read on SIGHUP; add snippet to SDK docs showing how to reinitialize Client with new env var. Reference: /eng-infra/cloud-accounts-and-networking/key-rotation-playbook.

- Issue 2: Large-response streaming stalls for long generated outputs
  - Symptom: Streaming endpoint stops after ~60-90s on long token streams.
  - Root cause: Default HTTP client idle-timeout in customer infra (NLB / proxy) closes connection.
  - Canonical fix: Recommend using chunked transfer encoding / set proxy idle timeouts >= 5 minutes. Add sample NGINX / ALB timeout configs. Provide fallback: non-streaming paged completions with page tokens.

- Issue 3: Embedding mismatches between SDK and REST call (different vector norms)
  - Symptom: Vector similarity scores differ between embeddings created via SDK and curl.
  - Root cause: SDK applied L2-normalization by default for backward compatibility; REST endpoint defaults changed in model rollout.
  - Canonical fix: Document normalization behavior in SDK and add parameter normalize=true/false to the embeddings API. Update quickstart and add migration notes.

- Issue 4: High latency on cold-start for dedicated/private deployments
  - Symptom: First request after deploy experiences 3-6s extra latency.
  - Root cause: JIT/model cache population and kernel warm-up on GPU nodes.
  - Canonical fix: Recommend warm-up script (2-3 short prefix requests) in deployment docs and include kubectl job example for private deployments.

Support triage template (to include on each support-facing doc):
1. Symptom (exact error/log lines)
2. Affected SDKs / endpoints / versions
3. Reproduction steps (minimal curl example)
4. Temporary workaround (if any)
5. Permanent fix and PR/reference (link to code or docs)
6. Owner and ETA for customer fix

Release checklist for docs changes (minor/patch):
- Update page and changelog entry
- Run code snippet smoke tests in CI (script: tools/docs/smoke-test.sh)
- Assign reviewers and get approvals
- Merge and publish; notify #devex-docs channel
- Monitor support tickets for 72 hours for regressions

Rollback procedure for broken examples:
1. Revert page to last known-good revision via Confluence page history.
2. Post incident note on the page with reason and rollback timestamp.
3. If code artifacts changed (examples in repo), revert the commit and open an urgent PR.

Related pages and references:
- eng-developer-experience/docs-site/developer-experience-docs-operating-procedures-2026
- eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/developer-experience-sdk-quickstarts-and-api-examples-2026
- eng-infra/cloud-accounts-and-networking/key-rotation-playbook

Appendix: common code snippets and CI smoke test
- smoke-test.sh (example):
  #!/usr/bin/env bash
  set -e
  python examples/chat_quickstart.py || { echo "Python quickstart failed"; exit 1; }
  node examples/chat_quickstart.js || { echo "Node quickstart failed"; exit 1; }
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"redwood-chat-1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"ping"}]}' | grep -q "ping" || { echo "Curl quickstart failed"; exit 1; }

Feedback and continuous improvement:
- Every published quickstart will be reviewed at 30 and 90 days for clarity and correctness.
- Track docs-driven support tickets in the weekly DevEx review; create follow-up tasks for persistent gaps.
